bullets.title: S&P 500 extends record-setting run with 9 consecutive gains; AVGO earnings tonight the key test
bullets.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,612 (+0.16%), marking its 9th straight session at all-time highs and 24th ATH YTD. The index rallied back from a -7% YTD hole in late March—one of history's strongest recoveries. Options put/call ratios hit decade-low 0.58, signaling max-bullish positioning that some observers warn could turn violent if sentiment shifts. AVGO reports after the close with a high bar—JPM raised the FY27 AI backlog estimate to $150B+ and Tomahawk 6 nearly sold out for FY27, but Citi notes 55% of investors expect AVGO to trade lower post-results.

bullets.title: US-Iran conflict escalates: crude surges to $95+, oil market tightening
bullets.body: US forces struck an Iranian tanker and a ground control station on Qeshm Island; Iran retaliated with ballistic missiles and drones targeting US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. WTI futures surged to ~$93-96/bbl (+2-4% overnight), a third consecutive day of gains. Traders warn prolonged Hormuz disruptions could push Brent to $104 in H2 with upside to $150. The US also drew down 9.1M barrels/week from strategic reserves—one of the largest weekly drops on record. OECD lowered global growth forecasts citing US-Iran war risks.

bullets.title: New US tariff broadside: 10-12.5% duties on 60+ countries over forced labor
bullets.body: The White House proposed 10% tariffs on Canada, Mexico, EU, Taiwan, and UK and 12.5% on China, Japan, India, South Korea, and Brazil—justified via USTR forced-labor investigations. The EU trade committee head rejected anything above 15% in the Turnberry framework. This adds to existing tariff uncertainty; ROTH and JPM both flagged the headline risk as a reason not to be max-long despite a tactical bullish stance.

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle still intact: hyperscalers spending $665B on IT infra this year
bullets.body: Multiple broker desks reiterated that AI demand is absorbing spare industry capacity. Hyperscalers are on track to spend $665B on IT infrastructure in 2026, with over 50% directed to AI. JPM notes AVGO's FY27 backlog jumped from $120B to $150B+; WSTS raised its 2026 semiconductor market forecast 90% to $1.51 trillion with memory up 250% YoY; and the NVDA/Computex ecosystem reinforced a multi-year capex cycle. IBM CEO flagged a $6-8T global AI capex commitment against only $1-2T of addressable annual revenue needed—but the market is treating near-term demand signals as the primary signal.

bullets.title: MRVL surges 32-45% on Jensen 'next trillion-dollar company' call; S&P 500 inclusion expected Friday
bullets.body: Jensen Huang called Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company' onstage at Computex in Taiwan alongside Marvell CEO Matt Murphy. MRVL closed up ~33% to $290.79 and was up another 12% premarket. JPM analyst notes ~9 standard deviation retail buying and a gamma squeeze in Friday 300/320 calls. An S&P 500 inclusion announcement is expected Friday, with index buyers heavily involved. MRVL raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $11.5B and outer-year to $16.5B, with interconnect revenue guided 70%+ growth.

bullets.title: Semiconductor rally extreme: semis trading 73% above 200-day MA, largest premium since Dot Com Bubble
bullets.body: The SOX index is up 110% since October, and semiconductor stocks now trade 73% above their 200-day moving average—the largest margin since the late 1990s. Semi customer inventory rose 5 days q/q but remains 6 days below peak, signaling early restocking. Wolfe flags destocking completed in 3Q25 with industry entering early restocking phase supported by AI demand absorbing spare capacity. WSTS's $1.51T forecast and Samsung's HBM5 announcement at Computex are additional positives.

bullets.title: Fed policy shift: Warsh signals potential rate guidance overhaul at June meeting; hires Project 2025 advisers
bullets.body: Multiple sources report Fed Chair Warsh may dial back forward guidance at the June meeting as soon as this week. Warsh hired two conservative policy veterans—Paul Winfree and Daniel Heil—as interim advisers; one authored the Fed's chapter in Project 2025. US job openings surged to a nearly 2-year high in the latest JOLTS data, with professional/business services openings jumping 668K (nearly double the prior record), reinforcing the case for rates staying higher for longer. 10-year Treasury yields rose 3bps to 4.48%.

bullets.title: ECB and BoE hiking cycles intact despite PMI weakness; euro area barely growing
bullets.body: Euro area May composite PMI revised to 48.5, implying ~0.3% annualized growth. ECB policymakers remain determined to hike in June and September to prevent de-anchoring of inflation expectations. UK composite PMI revised to 49.7 with services output prices hitting 60.6—the highest among major economies—as energy shock feeds through. Germany services PMI at 48.1, France and Italy flirting with stagnation; Spain holding ~2%.

bullets.title: Japan yields at multi-year highs across the curve: 10Y at 2.625%, 20Y at 3.535%
bullets.body: Japanese government bond yields rose sharply across all tenors overnight: 2Y to 1.40%, 5Y to 1.90%, 10Y to 2.625% (+6bps), 20Y to 3.535%, 30Y to 3.86%, and 40Y to 3.77%. PM Takaichi pledged FX cooperation with the US. Rising JGB yields have global rate implications and may pressure dollar/yen carry trades and risk appetite.

bullets.title: Gold surpasses US Treasuries as world's #2 central bank reserve asset
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirmed gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the second-largest central bank reserve asset globally. Combined with Bitcoin falling 47% since October (to a 2-month low near $66K) and crypto facing liquidity competition from the SpaceX IPO, the macro backdrop shows significant divergence in safe-haven and risk asset preferences.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO imminent: $135/share, $1.75T valuation, trading June 12
bullets.body: SpaceX is planning to set IPO terms as soon as Wednesday, targeting 555.6M shares at $135/share for a ~$1.75T valuation (down from >$2T earlier targets). Formal marketing starts June 4, pricing June 11, trading June 12 under ticker $SPCX. Elon Musk faces a 366-day lockup. Morningstar values SpaceX at $780B and warns the stock may be overvalued at IPO prices north of $1.5T. Multiple analysts flagged SpaceX's satellite broadband as a secular disruption threat to cable and legacy telecom.

bullets.title: Private equity liquidity stress: Partners Group withdrawal cap sparks 5-7% selloff in PE stocks; Cliffwater gates at 17% redemptions
bullets.body: KKR, ARES, BX, and APO all fell 5-7% premarket following a Partners Group evergreen fund redemption cap. Separately, Cliffwater Private Credit Fund gated investors for the second straight quarter after 17% redemption requests. These events signal stress in semi-liquid private credit and infrastructure vehicles that may not be isolated incidents.

bullets.title: PANW beats Q3 cleanly; organic growth debate caps stock despite 60% NGS ARR growth
bullets.body: Palo Alto Networks delivered Q3 revenue of $3.0B (+2% vs. consensus), EPS $0.85 (+7.6%), NGS ARR +60% YoY to $8.13B, and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $11.42-11.43B. Acquisitions (CyberArk, Chronosphere) drove ~$180M of the ARR beat. Stock fell ~3% afterhours as investors questioned whether organic guidance was raised beyond the F3Q beat and whether Mythos AI security budget inflection is visible in FY27. Street is 80% Buy; average PT raised to $295, but Citi maintains $210 and ROTH $210.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples expanded +7% WoW but IGV still -3.8% YTD vs S&P 500 +11.2% YTD
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index recovered to 5.4x FY+2 EV/Sales after +7.1% WoW multiple expansion, and the security index recovered to 7.6x (+4.9% WoW). Despite the bounce, IGV is -3.8% YTD versus the S&P at +11.2%, reflecting the sector's underperformance versus the broader market. Goldman desk noted flows chasing Mag7 supply more than software on Tuesday.

bullets.title: Tech capex-productivity correlation strengthens; private capex leads nonfarm productivity by 3 years
bullets.body: Piper Sandler and PSC Macro both flagged that private capex has a 90% correlation with nonfarm productivity, leading by 3 years. Current tech capex cycle (predating GPT era) is broadly boosting productivity, margins, profits, and potential GDP. R&D investments in place point to productivity returning to early-2000s highs in coming quarters—a structural bull case for the sector.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera CPU targets $20B market; 80% faster than x86 for agentic AI
bullets.body: At Computex GTC Taipei, NVIDIA launched the Vera CPU—80% faster than x86 on agentic task completion—and said it targets a $20B standalone CPU TAM. Agent demand went from zero to massive in 6 months. NVDA also announced N1X (RTX Spark) for AI PCs running 120B parameter LLMs with 128GB LPDDR5X memory (vs. 12-16GB average), and extended its 50% FCF return policy into perpetuity. ARM gained $60B in market cap on the same Computex news flow.

bullets.title: US retail traffic deceleration in May: +1.0% YoY vs +3.4% in Q1; consumer spending softening
bullets.body: Citi's retail traffic tracker showed May overall +1.0% YoY, a sharp deceleration from Q1's +3.4%. Citi credit card data also showed May overall spending +1.2% YoY vs. Q1 -0.4%, with electronics accelerating sharply (+6.8% vs. -3.5% in Q1) but apparel and department stores weakening. Thor Industries cut FY26 EPS guidance by $0.45 and cited 'low consumer confidence from inflation and geopolitical events' as towable RV demand falls 25% YoY. Goldman CEO Solomon said markets are in 'greed' mode, and noted inflation is a bigger near-term focus than employment.

bullets.title: EU Tech Sovereignty Package and Chips Act 2.0 launch June 3; MSFT data sovereignty threat structural but gradual
bullets.body: Brussels unveiled a sweeping digital sovereignty plan on June 3 including EU Chips Act 2.0 prioritizing photonics. Separately, a Jefferies note flagged a structural but gradual risk to Microsoft's moat as EU governments migrate workloads off Teams/Office/Azure onto sovereign alternatives—France migrating 2.5M civil servants to Visio, Germany's Schleswig-Holstein moving 30k workstations off MSFT, Denmark switching to LibreOffice. US CLOUD Act exposure is the key concern; TCI Fund reportedly reducing MSFT exposure.

bullets.title: ChatGPT hits 1B monthly active users; MSFT Build launches 7 AI models, Majorana 2 quantum chip
bullets.body: ChatGPT reached 1 billion monthly active users in record time. Microsoft's Build conference unveiled 7 new MAI models (including reasoning and coding-focused), Project Solara agentic platform, Scout AI assistant, Majorana 2 quantum chip targeting 2029 commercialization (1,000x reliability improvement), and announced Maia 200 custom silicon achieving 1.4x performance/watt vs. Nvidia GB200. MSFT added more Azure data center capacity in the last 18 months than its first decade.

bullets.title: AAPL WWDC June 8: Gemini-based Siri overhaul expected as key catalyst; stock historically +11% June-September
bullets.body: JPM and GS both highlighted WWDC on June 8 as a catalyst, with a major Siri overhaul expected—Gemini-based standalone chatbot app, 'Search or Ask' in Dynamic Island, multi-command support, and personal context awareness. Foldable iPhone and touch-screen Mac are expected in 2H26. Apple shares historically outperform the S&P by ~11% average in the June-September period. JPM maintains Overweight.
